hpi: {{patient_name}} is a neonate presenting with seizures, poor feeding, vomiting, lethargy, and urine/cerumen that smells like maple syrup (burnt sugar). MSUD is an autosomal recessive inborn error of metabolism — deficiency of branched-chain alpha-ketoacid dehydrogenase complex → accumulation of branched-chain amino acids (leucine, isoleucine, valine) and their ketoacids. Leucine is neurotoxic → encephalopathy, seizures. Newborn screening detects elevated leucine. Diagnosis: plasma amino acids — markedly elevated leucine, isoleucine, valine. Urine organic acids: branched-chain ketoacids. During acute decompensation: remove leucine (dialysis if severe), provide calories (glucose + insulin to promote anabolism), correct electrolyte abnormalities. Long-term: dietary restriction of BCAAs with special formula, liver transplant for severe cases.
